# The Teleporter keeps its old target while another weapon's shot waits (851-3463, docs/quirks.md §1), and the
# wiki clip quirks/teleporter-old-target. A staged scene (written by wiki-clips --replays from a scene spec,
# docs/wiki-media.md): it boots, loads this custom level from the title's load-level menu (240), and plays the
# scene's inputs from 241, its frame 0. The player (@) stands between a Teleporter (?) and a Shotgun (=), a
# brick (1) beside the Teleporter:
#   1111111111111111111111
#   1000000000000000000001  (ten rows of this)

#   1111111111111111111111

# He picks up the Teleporter (259) and uses it with up held (272): it sets tx and ty, 4 blocks above him,
# (153, 136), and moves him there; he falls back. He puts it down (327), picks up the Shotgun (361) and fires
# it to the right (371), which sets firing to 40, a wait the step counts down. He puts the Shotgun down (379),
# picks the Teleporter up again (399) and uses it facing left (405), with firing still 6: scrUseItem's
# sideways branches pick a new spot only if firing == 0, which the Teleporter never sets, so tx and ty are
# still the last use's, and he's moved up to (153, 136) again, not 4 to 8 blocks left. Used facing left once
# the wait is over (441), it moves him 5 blocks left, to (73, 200). Before any use with tx set, the same use
# reads the unset tx, a GML error that stops the game (port and oracle alike).
